title: A screen of random worlds, round 2

thesis.claim: Fifty more worlds drawn as round 1's were, with a new round seed, meet the same two walls: at iteration 2,000 no drawn world is at once resilient, a true space, as diverse as B2's median world in its agents and its decisions, and no more even than B2's least even world.
thesis.why: In round 1 (Experiment 38), of the 22 drawn worlds that lived to 2,000, 15 were spaces that a single loss could cut, 2 were resilient but folded, and 4 were neither. The one world both resilient and a space (world 46, the estate paid to the newborns) had agents alike in their staking and tokens too even. One rule at a time showed the same: mending keeps a world whole and folds it, and estates that pay for births keep it a space and fill it with paupers. A round drawn the same way should meet the same walls. The author chose to draw round 2 as round 1 was drawn and to judge both rounds together, since round 1 had a single interesting world to set values aside by.
thesis.confirm: No drawn world of round 2 meets the four criteria resilient, almost three-dimensional, diverse and not too even together at 2,000 (research/screen/judge.py E38 E39, with B2's lines from Experiment 16's ten worlds).
thesis.refute: At least one does: the page says which world, what else it misses if anything, and which of its settings set it apart.
